tweet_summary: Turkish-language post by 'KABAC' (862k views) presents night footage of urban destruction/rescue as 'images of the ruins of Tel Aviv struck by Iranian missiles,' mocking Israeli civilian-casualty appeals. Video OCR shows an IRGC ('sepah_pasdaran') watermark; frames show rescue workers, fire trucks, a crushed vehicle, and a heavily damaged building.
why_note_decision: A note is warranted: the footage is misattributed. The severe building-collapse destruction shown is consistent with the March 1, 2026 Iranian missile strike on Beit Shemesh (Ramat Lehi neighborhood) that destroyed the Tiferet Israel synagogue and killed nine — NOT Tel Aviv, where damage from that salvo was far more limited (a building hit, one killed, broken glass/debris). Calling this 'the ruins of Tel Aviv' overstates Tel Aviv damage and mislocates a real Beit Shemesh tragedy. (A notorious fully AI-generated 'Tel Aviv destroyed' video also circulated in this period, so location/authenticity claims about such clips need care.)
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note corrects the LOCATION mislabeling: the heavy-destruction footage is not Tel Aviv but matches the March 1, 2026 Iranian missile strike on Beit Shemesh (synagogue destroyed, 9 killed), while Tel Aviv's damage from that attack was comparatively limited — sourced to a reliable outlet (Times of Israel / Al Jazeera / Euronews / BBC / NYT / Amnesty). Written in Turkish is appropriate given the tweet's language. AVOID the original note's failure (rated notHelpfulOpinionSpeculation 8, Incorrect 7, SourcesMissingOrUnreliable 5): do NOT assert the precise Beit-Shemesh identification with unwarranted confidence if the clip cannot be verified — a separate AI-generated 'Tel Aviv destroyed' fake also circulated, so a note that confidently authenticates the WRONG clip should fail. The note must ground its Beit-Shemesh ID in the destruction/casualty evidence and not merely swap one unsourced location for another. A note that accepts the 'Tel Aviv ruins' framing, or that calls all such footage AI without basis, fails.

original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Direction is correct (real footage misattributed: Beit Shemesh, not Tel Aviv) and sources are solid (NYT/BBC/Euronews), but rated NOT_HELPFUL (16 ratings; dominant notHelpfulOpinionSpeculation 8, Incorrect 7, SourcesMissingOrUnreliable 5). The note asserts the Beit-Shemesh identification confidently, but the specific clip is hard to verify from the frames (and an AI-generated 'Tel Aviv destroyed' fake circulated simultaneously), so raters split on whether the relabeling was proven. The NYT source is paywalled.

fact_check.notes: March 1, 2026 Iranian salvo: heaviest destruction in Beit Shemesh (Ramat Lehi) — Tiferet Israel synagogue destroyed, 9 killed, ~46 injured, ~500m damage radius. Tel Aviv: a building struck, 1 killed, far lighter damage. The IRGC ('sepah_pasdaran') watermark and the real rescue-worker/fire-truck frames indicate genuine strike footage relabeled as 'Tel Aviv ruins.' CAVEAT: a separate fully AI-generated 'Tel Aviv destroyed' video also went viral days later (HonestReporting/Algemeiner), so I cannot fully confirm THIS clip is the real Beit Shemesh footage vs. another misattributed/AI clip from the AI frame description alone — but either way the 'ruins of Tel Aviv' label is false.

importance.lens_rationale: 862k impressions of war footage relabeled to overstate destruction of a major city; misattributed/AI war imagery distorting casualty and damage perception is a high-volume conflict-misinformation pattern with civic stakes.
